expected_behavior: LAB-005 computes 5-session forward excess return vs BENCH-001 (SPY): R_stock(t,h) - R_benchmark(t,h)
actual_behavior: LAB-005 was set identical to LAB-004 (absolute return) via direct assignment: lab005 = lab004
root_cause: In scripts/phase12d_run.py line 151, the label was set as: lab005 = lab004  # Same data for now. The correct implementation exists in src/orbit/ml/phase11_1_labels.py (compute_excess_return_label) but was never called in the Phase 12D execution script.
failure_mechanism: Direct Python variable aliasing. lab005 pointed to the same LabelSnapshot object as lab004. Both contained absolute forward returns with no benchmark subtraction.
why_tests_did_not_detect: Phase 12D run script tested pipeline completion, not label value correctness
No regression test existed to verify LAB-005 != LAB-004 at the value level
The test in test_phase10_adversarial.py checked label_id strings, not actual values
The Phase 11.1 tests (test_phase11_1.py) tested the compute_excess_return_label function in isolation but it was never integrated into the Phase 12D pipeline

earlier_phases_affected.phase_11_2: Phase 11.2 used the correct compute_excess_return_label via phase11_2_benchmark.py
earlier_phases_affected.phase_9: Phase 9 only used LAB-004 (absolute return) - not affected

historical_impact.phase_12d_lab004: VALID - absolute return results are correct
historical_impact.phase_12d_lab005: INVALID - these are absolute returns mislabeled as excess returns
historical_impact.phase_12d_comparison: INVALID - LAB-004 vs LAB-005 comparison is meaningless

corrective_action: Create LAB-006 v1 as the corrected excess-return label (preserving LAB-005 historical artifact)
Use compute_excess_return_label from phase11_1_labels.py with BENCH-001 SPY data
Re-run only affected experiments (all LAB-005 experiments from Phase 12D)
regression_test: Assert that LAB-006 values differ from LAB-004 values for >1% of observations
